summary: Dubstep (UK, 140 halftime): kick on 1 and a big snare on 3 at 138-142 BPM, shuffled hats, a heavy sine or square sub with a wobbling mid bass above it, dark minor pads, sparse eerie leads, dub space; knowledge/style/dubstep.json is its template
body: Tempo 140 BPM (135-145), felt in half time at 70: the kick on 1 and the snare on 3, hats and percussion at full speed.

Drums: UK dubstep is sparse and dry, a lot of space between hits, shuffled or triplet hats and percussion; brostep is punchier, compressed and layered, with fills and rolls. A big, chunky snare (parallel compression, saturation).

Bass: the loudest part: a clean sine sub below 60-100 Hz, mono, holding the root, and a mid bass (square or saw, distorted) above it whose filter wobbles with an LFO synced at 1/4, 1/8 or 1/16; slow wobbles for UK and deep dubstep, fast and growling for brostep and riddim.
Harmony: minor and dark: i-VI, i-III-VII-VI, or one chord; held low pads with long reverb; melodic dubstep borrows the pop I-V-vi-IV.
Lead: sparse: an eerie square or bell line, a dub siren, a vocal or MC snippet; brostep adds vocal chops and hooks.
Texture/master: sub-heavy but spacious; dub reggae's long delays and reverbs on everything but the dry drums; brostep loud and full, every range occupied. No lofi roll-off.
Sources (2026-11-26): Mode Audio 'Dubstep: 5 Production Essentials'; Orphiq 'What Is Dubstep? Wobble Bass, 140 BPM, Subgenres'.

Apply: pattern/halftime-shuffle on the drums, then pattern/prog-dubstep-characteristic-1 on the keys four bars later. For a whole style change the Team Lead's restyle uses knowledge/style/dubstep.json instead.

drums.about: the drum track (a kit); leave out if there isn't one

keys.about: a chordal part (keys, pad); leave out if there isn't one

key.about: the project's key; leave out to estimate it from the notes
